description.text: We are one of the largest independent petroleum refiners and suppliers of unbranded transportation fuels, heating oil, petrochemical feedstocks, lubricants and other petroleum products in the United States. We sell our products throughout the Northeast, Midwest, Gulf Coast and West Coast of the United States, as well as in other regions of the United States, Canada and Mexico and are able to ship products to other international destinations. We own and operate six domestic oil refineries and related assets and own a 50% interest in the Renewable Diesel Facility through our SBR equity method investment. Our refineries have a combined processing capacity, known as throughput, of approximately 1,000,000 bpd, and a weighted-average Nelson Complexity Index of 12.8 based on current operating conditions. The complexity and throughput capacity of our refineries are subject to change dependent upon configuration changes we make to respond to market conditions, as well as a result of investments made to improve our facilities and maintain compliance with environmental and governmental regulations. We operate in two reportable business segments: Refining and Logistics. Our six oil refineries are all engaged in the refining of crude oil and other feedstocks into petroleum products, and represent the Refining segment. PBFX operates certain logistical assets such as crude oil and refined products terminals, pipelines, and storage facilities, which represent the Logistics segment.

about.description_short: PBF Energy Inc. (NYSE: PBF) is one of the largest independent refiners in North America, operating, through its subsidiaries, oil refineries and related facilities in California, Delaware, Louisiana, New Jersey and Ohio. Our mission is to operate our facilities in a safe, reliable and environmentally responsible manner, provide employees with a safe and rewarding workplace, become a positive influence in the communities where we do business and provide superior returns to our investors. PBF Energy is also a 50% partner in the St. Bernard Renewables joint venture focused on the production of next generation sustainable fuels.

analysis_md:
# PBF — PBF Energy Inc.
Pass-1 run, 2026-10-19. Price $81.26 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap $9,338,034,586 — in scope under $40B.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed — except where a company release or cited reporting is named as the source.

## What it is
One of the largest U.S. independent refiners: six refineries (Delaware City and Paulsboro on the East Coast, Toledo in the Mid-Continent, Chalmette on the Gulf Coast, Torrance and Martinez on the West Coast) with combined throughput capacity of roughly 1 million barrels per day and a combined Nelson Complexity Index of about 12.8, plus a 50% stake in the St. Bernard Renewables renewable-diesel JV. Revenue is refined-product sales recognized on delivery — a crude-price pass-through, so the revenue line moves with oil, not with volume or pricing power.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow −$78,000,000; capex $705,200,000 (PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, rollup — the whole filed capex line); SBC $39,000,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: −$822,200,000 = −$7.15/share** (base_oe_latest_per_share −$7.154821647099987 in dcf_numbers.json).
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): −$31,400,000 total — less negative only because it caps the capex deduction at D&A ($371,600,000) in a year when actual capex was $705,200,000, much of it the Martinez rebuild; the conservative OCF-based figure is the honest one here.
- OE positive 3 of the last 5 fiscal years. OE/share history tells the cycle plainly: $1.57 (2021), $32.20 (2022 supercycle), $4.81 (2023), −$3.35 (2024), −$7.15 (2025).
- Net debt at FY2025 end: $1,620,400,000 (long-term debt $2,148,300,000 less cash $527,900,000; lease liabilities a further $727,400,000). Per the Q2 2026 release, net debt then fell by over $1.4B in that single quarter to roughly $855M (debt $1.75B, cash $894.1M) — deleveraging funded by the blowout quarter discussed below, not by the normalized base.
- **Base used = the engine's normalized base: median of the last 3 FY OE/share = −$3.35/share** (base_oe_per_share −$3.3455266308488105, base_source median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). The three median-window years are 2023 (+$4.81), 2024 (−$3.35, industry-wide weak margins) and 2025 (−$7.15, the Martinez fire year: the 157k bpd refinery — ~16% of system capacity — was idled by the February 1, 2025 fire and only returned to full operations in May 2026).

**TTM was built and rejected as the base (see STALE_FY under Flags).** ttm.py through Q2 2026 (ttm.json):
- OCF: FY −$78,000,000 − prior YTD −$470,300,000 + current YTD $1,265,100,000 = **TTM $1,657,400,000**
- Capex: FY $705,200,000 − prior YTD $267,100,000 + current YTD $476,500,000 = **TTM $914,600,000**
- SBC: FY $39,000,000 − prior YTD $21,400,000 + current YTD $17,400,000 = **TTM $35,000,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **120,603,759**
- **TTM OE total $707,800,000 → $5.87/share** (ttm_oe_per_share $5.868805465673752)
- Why rejected: the TTM window straddles two opposite extremes and neither is a run rate. Its first three quarters were fire-depressed; its entire profit sits in Q2 2026 alone (quarterly OCF $1,588,800,000 and net income attributable to PBF of $906,400,000, per fundamentals.json), a quarter in which (i) crack spreads hit records on Middle East hostilities trapping crude and products with millions of barrels/day of global refining capacity offline — diesel cracks topped $100/bbl for the first time in 2026; (ii) results included a **$250.0 million insurance-recovery gain** on the Martinez fire, the fifth unallocated installment, received in the quarter (cumulative recoveries $1.25B); and (iii) the CFO put the quarter's **working-capital benefit at approximately $430 million** inside its ~$1.6B of operating cash flow. The insurance receipt and the WC benefit together are $680M against a TTM OE total of $707,800,000 — strip two non-recurring items from one quarter and the TTM base is approximately zero. Capitalizing that as a DCF base at a price near its highs would be the classic peak-earnings trap; the same discipline was applied to the other refiner in this sweep (DINO). The TTM figure remains the bull-case anchor — see Thoughts.

## Moat: 3/10 — weak
Justification: a price-taking commodity refiner. The edges are locational and complexity-based and soften the cycle; they have never repealed it.
- FOR: Six-refinery ~1M bpd system, Nelson complexity ~12.8 — complex cracking units convert discounted heavy crude into higher-value gasoline and diesel.
- FOR: Scarce West Coast capacity — Martinez (157k bpd, restarted May 2026) and Torrance in a California market importing ~250k bpd, roughly a third of its gasoline demand, as in-state competitors close.
- FOR: Geographic spread (East/Gulf/Mid-Continent/West Coast) and crude-slate flexibility capture regional differentials; St. Bernard Renewables JV income (Q2 2026 net income from SBR $27.5M) and the RBI program targeting >$350M of run-rate cost savings by end-2026.
- AGAINST: Pure price-taker on both sides — crude in, commodity fuels out; crack spreads are set globally and geopolitically, as the war-driven 2026 spike proves in both directions.
- AGAINST: No pricing power, switching costs or network effects. ROIC evidence (fundamentals.json roic_proxy): 9.1% / 11.2% / 7.5% / 11.8% in the normal years 2016–19, 74.1% (2022) and 37.2% (2023) on exogenous spreads, −23.8% (2020), −8.5% (2024), −0.6% (2025); gross margin 10.0% (2022) → −1.1% (2024) → −1.9% (2025). Through-cycle ROIC hovers near the cost of capital and goes deeply negative in downcycles.
- AGAINST: Capital intensity and turnaround load (capex $705,200,000 in FY2025; 2026 guidance $825–875M; turnarounds at most refineries in 2026), RFS/RIN compliance costs ($331.3M in Q2 2026 alone, more than double a year earlier), California regulatory exposure and long-run U.S. gasoline demand decline.
- A 3 gives CAP = 5.9 years (dcf_numbers.json cap_years) — moot on a negative base, recorded for consistency.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-19)
Probabilities 15/30/30/15/10 (bear-tilted vs the 10/25/30/25/10 default, per the OE_VOLATILE resolution below); default offsets −12/−5/0/+5/+12pp and OE multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25 retained. Growth blend is −8.18% (rev CAGR 5y +14.18%, 3y −14.44%, latest YoY −11.42%, plus the +3.24pp buyback adjustment) — unusable in any case, because:
- **No scenario table exists for this name, by design:** with a normalized base OE of −$3.35/share and latest-FY −$7.15/share, the engine produces no IV@15% and no implied IRR in any scenario — super bear through super bull all scale a negative base.
- **Tier by numbers: F** (F sub-type: no_cash_generation — the sum of the last 3 fiscal years' OCF − capex is not positive). Probability-weighted IV/IRR: not emitted (null in dcf_numbers.json).

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago): ttm.py was run and its legs are quoted in full above. The TTM base (+$5.87/share) was **not** pinned, with the written reason given there: it is one war-driven blowout quarter carrying a $250M insurance receipt and a ~$430M working-capital benefit on top of three fire-depressed quarters — a peak print, not a normalized base. The normalized median base is retained, so the F does not depend on ignoring the TTM; it depends on the TTM not being capitalizable, and even the through-cycle record (OE/share $3.09–$4.16 in the normal years 2016–19) would be a sub-5% yield at $81.26.
- **BUYBACK_TAILWIND** (share count shrinking 3.2%/yr): filed diluted counts fell 130,509,448 (2023) → 117,111,607 (2024) → 114,915,513 (2025), and the +3.24pp growth adjustment already credits it. Note the tailwind has stalled: the H1 2026 YTD diluted count in ttm.json is 120,603,759, above the FY2025 count. Moot on a negative base either way.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT** (>60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs): not a divestiture, M&A or restatement — it is crude-price pass-through. Revenue went $27,253,400,000 (2021) → $46,830,300,000 (2022) on the post-invasion crude spike, then normalized to $38,324,800,000 (2023), $33,115,300,000 (2024) and $29,332,300,000 (2025). No CAGR straddling that spike was used for any growth input (the base is negative, so none was used at all). The one structural change in the window, the St. Bernard Renewables JV (50%, equity-method, from 2023), does not break the consolidated OCF series' comparability for this purpose.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x): real and definitional — this is a cyclical refiner. OE/share ran $1.57 / $32.20 / $4.81 / −$3.35 / −$7.15 over 2021–25. Handled the only way available on a negative normalized base: probabilities were bear-tilted to 15/30/30/15/10, and the verdict is sized to the conservative (normalized) end rather than the peak TTM.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (net income vs OCF differ by >40% in 2023, 2024): working-capital swings plus non-cash addbacks, both visible in financials_history.csv. 2023: net income $2,140,500,000 vs OCF $1,338,500,000 — the gap is the $1,453,800,000 working-capital build (delta_nwc) in a high-price year, partly offset by D&A of $314,400,000 and SBC of $51,500,000 added back. 2024: net loss −$533,800,000 vs OCF +$43,400,000 — D&A of $358,300,000 added back and a $214,100,000 working-capital inflow (delta_nwc −$214,100,000) bridge most of it. The conservative OE series is built from OCF and deducts SBC separately, so the divergence does not contaminate the base; it is the normal refinery pattern of inventory/receivable values tracking crude prices.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the range across bases: normalized median −$3.35/share (Tier F), latest FY −$7.15/share, TTM +$5.87/share — and the TTM's entire total is explained by two non-recurring Q2 2026 items ($250M insurance + ~$430M WC benefit = $680M vs TTM OE of $707,800,000) inside a record, war-driven crack-spread quarter. Anyone quoting the TTM as a run rate is hiding the ball.
- Price context matters: the shares ran roughly +189% in 2026 to $81.26, near the top of the cited 52-week range of $25.62–$82.61 — the market has already capitalized the margin spike and the Martinez restart (completed May 2026). Q3 2026 throughput guidance of 900,000–960,000 bpd and management's tight-inventories argument may keep cracks elevated into 2027; that is a trading case on geopolitics, not an owner's-earnings case at a 15% hurdle.
- What would change the verdict: a filed full year of positive OE at normalized (not record) crack spreads with Martinez running — i.e., proof that the mid-cycle base has reset above zero after the RBI cost program (>$350M run-rate savings targeted by end-2026). Even at the pre-2020 normal-years level of ~$3–4/share of OE, $81.26 would not clear 15%; the hurdle-clearing price on any defensible normalized base is a fraction of the current price, so no single hurdle price is quoted.
- Balance sheet is the one genuinely improved item: Q2 2026 cash generation cut net debt to roughly $855M per the company release (from $1,620,400,000 at FY2025 end on the filed basis) — survivability through the next downcycle is better than it was, which supports the business, not the price.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: F** (no positive normalized owner's earnings — median base −$3.35/share, latest FY −$7.15/share; the only positive base, TTM +$5.87/share, is a peak-cycle print built on non-recurring insurance and working-capital items)
- Confidence: **Medium** (high on the filed arithmetic and on the TTM's composition; medium overall because refining margins can stay extreme longer than any model assumes, and a second straight blowout year would force a base re-think)
- One-liner: Pure cyclical refiner, moat 3/10 — owner's earnings are negative on the normalized base (−$3.35/sh median; latest FY −$7.15/sh) after the Martinez fire year and weak 2024 margins, and the positive TTM figure (+$5.87/sh) is one war-driven blowout quarter carrying a $250M insurance receipt and a ~$430M working-capital benefit, not a run rate; at $81.26, near the top of a ~189% 2026 run, no positive normalized base exists to clear the 15% hurdle.
